Confidence intervals for
multiple correlation
are generated using
the `RSqSandwich()` function from the `betaSandwich` package.
In this example,
we use the data set and the model used in
[betaSandwich: Example Using the BetaHC Function](example-beta-sandwich.html).


``` r
library(package = betaSandwich)
```




``` r
df <- betaSandwich::nas1982
```

## Fit the regression model using the `lm()` function.


``` r
object <- stats::lm(formula = QUALITY ~ NARTIC + PCTGRT + PCTSUPP, data = df)
```

## Estimate the standardized regression slopes and the corresponding sampling covariance matrix.

### Multivariate Normal-Theory Approach


``` r
std_mvn <- BetaN(object = object)
```

#### Asymptotic Distribution-Free Approach


``` r
std_adf <- BetaADF(object = object)
```

#### HC3


``` r
std_hc3 <- BetaHC(object = object, type = "hc3")
```

## Estimate the multiple correlation coefficients (R-squared and adjusted R-squared) and the corresponding sampling covariance matrix.

The R-squared and the adjusted R-squared are
$R^{2} = \boldsymbol{\beta}^{\ast\prime} \boldsymbol{R}_{x} \boldsymbol{\beta}^{\ast}$
and
$\bar{R}^{2} = 1 - \left( 1 - R^{2} \right) \left( n - 1 \right) / \left( n - k \right)$,
where $\boldsymbol{\beta}^{\ast}$ is the vector of standardized slopes,
$\boldsymbol{R}_{x}$ is the correlation matrix of the regressors,
$n$ is the sample size,
and $k$ is the number of parameters of the regression model, including the intercept.
The sampling covariance matrix is obtained by the delta method
from the sampling covariance matrix of the standardized parameters.


``` r
mvn <- RSqSandwich(object = std_mvn, alpha = 0.05)
adf <- RSqSandwich(object = std_adf, alpha = 0.05)
hc3 <- RSqSandwich(object = std_hc3, alpha = 0.05)
```

## Methods

### summary

Summary of the results of `RSqSandwich()`.


``` r
summary(object = mvn)
#> Call:
#> RSqSandwich(object = std_mvn, alpha = 0.05)
#> 
#> R-squared and adjusted R-squared with MVN standard errors:
#>        est     se       z p   2.5%  97.5%
#> rsq 0.8045 0.0517 15.5608 0 0.7032 0.9059
#> adj 0.7906 0.0554 14.2713 0 0.6820 0.8991
summary(object = adf)
#> Call:
#> RSqSandwich(object = std_adf, alpha = 0.05)
#> 
#> R-squared and adjusted R-squared with MVN standard errors:
#>        est     se       z p   2.5%  97.5%
#> rsq 0.8045 0.0519 15.4910 0 0.7027 0.9063
#> adj 0.7906 0.0556 14.2073 0 0.6815 0.8996
summary(object = hc3)
#> Call:
#> RSqSandwich(object = std_hc3, alpha = 0.05)
#> 
#> R-squared and adjusted R-squared with HC3 standard errors:
#>        est     se       z p   2.5%  97.5%
#> rsq 0.8045 0.0573 14.0286 0 0.6921 0.9169
#> adj 0.7906 0.0614 12.8662 0 0.6701 0.9110
```

### coef

Calculate R-squared and adjusted R-squared.


``` r
stats::coef(object = mvn)
#>       rsq       adj 
#> 0.8045263 0.7905638
stats::coef(object = adf)
#>       rsq       adj 
#> 0.8045263 0.7905638
stats::coef(object = hc3)
#>       rsq       adj 
#> 0.8045263 0.7905638
```

### vcov

Calculate the sampling covariance matrix of R-squared and adjusted R-squared.


``` r
stats::vcov(object = mvn)
#>             rsq         adj
#> rsq 0.002673125 0.002864062
#> adj 0.002864062 0.003068638
stats::vcov(object = adf)
#>             rsq         adj
#> rsq 0.002697266 0.002889927
#> adj 0.002889927 0.003096351
stats::vcov(object = hc3)
#>             rsq         adj
#> rsq 0.003288894 0.003523815
#> adj 0.003523815 0.003775516
```

### confint

Generate confidence intervals for R-squared and adjusted R-squared.


``` r
stats::confint(object = mvn, level = 0.95)
#>         2.5 %    97.5 %
#> rsq 0.7031917 0.9058608
#> adj 0.6819911 0.8991366
stats::confint(object = adf, level = 0.95)
#>         2.5 %    97.5 %
#> rsq 0.7027351 0.9063174
#> adj 0.6815019 0.8996258
stats::confint(object = hc3, level = 0.95)
#>         2.5 %    97.5 %
#> rsq 0.6921245 0.9169280
#> adj 0.6701334 0.9109943
```
